plan.estimand: Minimum total development sample size for continuous prediction model meeting Riley precision criteria
plan.hypothesis: Prediction model performance will stabilize with adequate sample size such that optimism (apparent R-squared minus adjusted R-squared) ≤ 0.05 and parameter estimates shrink to stable values with target shrinkage 0.90

parameters.name: Maximum absolute optimism (apparent minus adjusted R-squared)
Residual SD multiplicative margin of error
Mean outcome multiplicative margin of error

assumptions: Outcome is normally distributed with constant variance
Linear relationship between predictors and outcome
Anticipated adjusted R-squared 0.20 is realistic for this population and predictor set
Shrinkage 0.90 represents expected optimism in parameter estimation from model development to external validation
Precision criteria (optimism ≤0.05, multiplicative margins 1.1) are appropriate for this model's intended use
Default pmsampsize package precision criteria are appropriate
Intercept and residual SD precision criteria apply to the specified multiplicative margins of error
missing_information: pmsampsize package version (user specified 1.1.3 in request, confirming availability and implementation details)
clarification_questions: Should the calculation prioritize the optimism criterion (maximum apparent-vs-adjusted R-squared difference 0.05) or the precision criteria (multiplicative margins 1.1 for intercept, residual SD, and mean outcome)? Riley methodology addresses both; if one is more critical to your use case, please confirm.

The shrinkage 0.90 represents internal-external validation slope—is this based on pilot data, subject matter knowledge, or a conservative assumption? This affects interpretation of the sample size recommendation.
scientific_notes: Riley et al. (2021) sample size guidance for prediction model development balances optimism in apparent performance against precision of key estimated quantities (intercept, residual SD, mean outcome) across a range of candidate predictors.
The pmsampsize package implements this framework; version 1.1.3 supports continuous, binary, and survival outcomes with flexible specification of shrinkage and precision targets.

The requested configuration (25 predictors, R² 0.20, shrinkage 0.90) represents a moderate-complexity model with expected internal optimism managed through planned statistical approach (e.g., cross-validation, regularization).
Multiplicative margins 1.1 are commonly used in precision planning for intercept and residual SD, representing ±10% relative precision around central estimates.
The maximum optimism criterion 0.05 (Nagelkerke scale) is standard in Riley guidance for continuous outcomes.
